properties.headline: Flood Watch issued August 31 at 4:35PM PDT until September 1 at 12:00AM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of northwest Arizona, including the following
area, Northwest Plateau.

* WHEN...Until midnight MST tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Thunderstorm activity will likely bring heavy rainfall that may
lead to flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued August 31 at 4:21PM CDT until September 2 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Texas, including the following
areas, Bolivar Peninsula, Chambers, Coastal Galveston, Coastal
Harris, Galveston Island, Inland Galveston, Inland Harris,
Montgomery, Northern Liberty, Polk, San Jacinto and Southern
Liberty.

* WHEN...From 1 AM CDT Tuesday through Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Periods of moderate to heavy rainfall associated with Tropical
Depression Five are expected to begin as early as late tonight
and lasting into late Tuesday night/early Wednesday morning. 3-5
inches with isolated amounts of 6-9 inches are expected with the
highest totals occuring east of I-45. Rainfall rates will exceed
3-4 inches per hour at times in the heaviest downpours, which can
lead to flash flooding especially in urban and vulnerable areas.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued August 31 at 11:51AM MST until August 31 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
The environment will remain conducive for additional showers and
thunderstorms through early this evening, mainly across La Paz,
northern Yuma and western Maricopa Counties. Training of storms could
lead to an additional 1 to 2 inches of rainfall causing rapid run-off
and flooding of low-water crossings and low-lying areas.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of south central Arizona, including the following
areas, Aguila Valley, Sonoran Desert Natl Monument and Tonopah
Desert.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Another round of showers and thunderstorms is likely during the
afternoon and evening hours. Heavy rainfall will be possible
which may cause localized flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued August 31 at 2:34AM MST until September 1 at 12:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...All of northern and central Arizona.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Raging
killer currents will be possible in side canyons and narrow slot
canyons. Low-water crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Showers and thunderstorms are expected to continue this afternoon
and evening. With deep monsoonal moisture in place and already
saturated soils in some locations, an elevated risk of flash
flooding will be in place through Monday.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Have a way to receive Flash Flood Warnings and be prepared to take
action should warnings be issued.

Consider changing your plans if you were going to hike, boat, or
paddleboard to a slot canyon or normally dry wash. If you do still
decide to recreate, check in at a nearby visitor center or ranger
station.
